title: Smoothed character sums and the analytic window hypothesis
summary: Defines ramp, Gchi, positive character families, their real weighted error Gm, and WindowHyp.

title: From compatible arithmetic data to a near-square-root error bound
summary: The core_gm statement gives the exact exponent 1/2 + (eD + eL + 7) eps; the final proof absorbs constants into x to the eps.

title: Quantified windows and the choice of epsilon
summary: States the order of quantifiers for window families and proves nonvanishing by choosing epsilon after the candidate real part is fixed.

title: Arbitrarily late power windows
summary: HasWindows requires whole intervals [Y,Y^la] arbitrarily far out; FormBAt turns the one-sided bound there into nonvanishing.

title: Assembling the character-specific nonvanishing input
summary: Connects host-supplied families to the arithmetic window bound and the analytic FormB criterion for each cyclic character level.

title: Identifying the arithmetic packet with an analytic character family
summary: Positive weights and level_family identify the two Gm definitions and their nonvanishing conclusions.

title: The Landau criterion for every arithmetic level
summary: Applies the general analytic theorem with delta = la - 1 and C = 1 after identifying the level family.

title: Power bounds on late windows imply nonvanishing
summary: The exact theorem takes 0 < theta < 1, delta > 0 and arbitrarily late window bounds Gm(y) <= C y^theta.

title: Converting a power bound into an integral majorant
summary: Chooses R(y) = |C| y^theta, whose weighted integral equals |C| delta log Y and is eventually at most Y^eta.

title: The analytic continuation and pole contract
summary: Defines the logarithmic-scale error, zero set, Laplace-transform continuation and nonzero pole residues, with positivity at real poles.

title: Why zeros give uncancelled poles
summary: Builds the transform from character and inverse-character contributions; positive weights and zero multiplicities make every residue nonzero.

title: Why one-sided control suffices
summary: Uses |g| + g <= 2R on the window and estimates the tails to bound a transform coefficient norm plus a real coefficient.

title: The windowed Landau pole-exclusion theorem
summary: Late windows bound high derivatives; nearest-pole asymptotics and Cauchy estimates contradict the resulting geometric growth rates.

title: Translating pole exclusion back to L-function nonvanishing
summary: Combines poleData and landau_window, using established nonvanishing on Re(s) >= 1 separately.

title: Extending from primitive characters to every character
summary: The inducing primitive L-function is nonzero, and every added Euler factor is nonzero because its subtracted term has norm less than one.

title: The arithmetic window and its cohomology bound
summary: Defines VVle, the character fields, admissible auxiliary primes, PageN, VAt and VWin. The bound controls weighted cohomology lengths throughout a suitably chosen interval.

title: The Galois cohomology module measured by shaLen
summary: Defines local data over primes above l, the inverse cyclotomic twist of Q_l/Z_l, the Sha submodule of first cohomology, and its Z_l-module length.

title: From the Galois representation input to VWin
summary: Passes the Row0b hypothesis, its OpenImageCondition wrapper and the imported base-change theorem to the automorphic window construction.

title: Four families of input to the arithmetic window
summary: Assembles local representation theory, automorphic/Galois statements, Galois cohomology and CM/abelian-variety statements into the literal automorphy theorem used for VWin.

title: The Galois input supplied to MainConclusion
summary: Supplies Row0b recT by applying galoisRepresentations_of_thetaLift to the imported theta-lifting theorem tLiftK.

title: The exact Galois representation contract Row0b
summary: Quantifies regular algebraic polarized cuspidal representations over CM fields and records continuous semisimple Galois representations, weight identities and restricted local comparison conditions.

title: Geometry, congruences and theta lifting feed the Galois theorem
summary: Defines recT by IsRecT and joins geometric seeds, congruences, trace limits, crystalline input and local compatibility to obtain Row0 and then Row0b.

title: Joining geometric realization to a theta lift
summary: Supplies the geometric realization theorem geoOne_holds to the construction that turns TLiftK into Row0b recT.

title: What the theta-lifting input actually asserts
summary: For the specified CM fields, Hermitian/skew spaces, compatible characters and weight inequalities, asserts the existence of a lift to sufficiently large rank.

title: The local correspondence laws used by recT
summary: Defines the Good cuspidal-support condition, the LawsT record for a map from irreducible GL representations to Weil-Deligne parameters, and universal local existence.

title: Assembling existence of the local correspondence
summary: Chooses an Artin map and cuspidal parameters, extends them using Langlands multisegments, and fills the LawsT fields using imported extension theorems.

title: The literature record and the nonvanishing assembly
summary: The three-field OpenLiteratureStatements record, construction of the dependency bundles, and the final EveryCharacter theorem.

title: From matched theta integrals to a compatible hypothesis witness
summary: Builds rational test vectors, a common evaluation grid, compatible functional and covolume conditions, and the final nonempty hypothesis record.

title: What agreement of theta integrals actually asserts
summary: Matching local and real models; convergence and decay; a unique nonzero proportionality constant; the quantified global agreement and local matching properties.

title: Concrete inequalities behind the geometric covolume estimate
summary: Recursive log-covolume control, orthogonal truncation, an exponentially small bad subspace, a polynomial slope ceiling, and a lower bound for the core slope.

title: The uniform covolume property required by the proof
summary: Defines tied points, the eventual uniformity across all points and lift stages, and CovolumeBoundOfX.

title: Arithmetic geometry supplies the covolume bound
summary: Uses resolution, principalisation, arithmetic Hilbert-Samuel, positivity, toroidal models and Hodge-bundle inputs to produce CovolumeBoundOfX.

title: How covering estimates combine into the covolume theorem
summary: Builds Gram and measure control, deep covers, height and degree estimates, a uniform slope lower bound, and the final covolume inequality.

title: Transporting the geometric bound to the chosen automorphic families
summary: Turns CovolumeBoundOfX into the linked third-place-series condition at the same extended parameters as the other inputs.

title: Building a complete compatible family of hypotheses
summary: Combines large unramified-exponent bundles with Galois estimates, functional conditions and the covolume bound to construct HypsAlt.

title: From compatible families and windows to EveryCharacter
summary: Produces TopG from the hypothesis witness and Green input, supplies each character using VWin, then passes from ZeroFreeAll to EveryCharacter.
